row.evidence: Microsoft documents no SCIM endpoint for Power BI; users are Microsoft Entra ID accounts (authentication "follows the Microsoft Entra auth code grant flow") and "Billing, License, and User administrators assign licenses to users" from the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Azure portal.
row.notes: New row. Power BI (now also sold inside Microsoft Fabric) has no SCIM service-provider endpoint of its own: every Power BI user is a Microsoft Entra ID account in the customer's tenant, so provisioning means creating the user in Entra ID (itself, or via Microsoft 365/Graph) and assigning a Power BI Pro or Premium Per User licence in the Microsoft 365 admin center or Azure portal. Other IdPs reach Power BI only through Entra ID (federation or Entra provisioning); there is no Power BI app in the Entra gallery or the Okta Integration Network. Scored like Azure DevOps: status none, idp.entra directory_sync to mark Entra-native identity, sso_plan Free because sign-in through the tenant's Entra ID (which can federate to the customer's own IdP) applies to every licence including the Fabric free account. Prices: Pro $14 and Premium Per User $24 per user/month paid yearly; PPU is also a $14 step-up add-on for Pro/E5 users; Pro is included in Microsoft 365 E5 and Office 365 E5. The Power BI REST API manages workspace access (add, update and remove users or groups per workspace, admin variants for Fabric administrators) and exposes the tenant activity (audit) log; user and licence creation itself is Microsoft Graph, scored under microsoft-365. Status none by absence.

plans.name: Fabric free account
plans.notes: Free licence; cannot share content. Sign-in via Entra ID applies to every licence.

scim.notes: No SCIM endpoint: Power BI users are Entra ID identities and licences are assigned in the Microsoft 365 admin center or Azure portal. Entra's inbound SCIM API and Graph belong to Microsoft 365/Entra, not Power BI.

capabilities.notes: The Power BI REST API grants, changes and removes workspace roles for users and groups and lists a user's item access; creating users and assigning licences is done in Entra ID / Microsoft Graph, not this API. Add Group User only grants workspace permissions to an existing identity.

endpoints.purpose: List users with access to a workspace
Grant a user or group a workspace role
Remove a user from a workspace
Admin: list items a user can access

audit_log_api.notes: Requires the Fabric administrator role or a service principal; no licence tier named.

rate_limits.text: Admin APIs: maximum 200 requests per hour.

user_api.notes: Workspace-access API, not an account lifecycle API. Plan gate is not stated on the API reference; the user API plan stays null.

okta.notes: https://www.okta.com/integrations/power-bi/ and /microsoft-power-bi/ return 404; Okta reaches Power BI only through its Microsoft Office 365 app into Entra ID (scored under microsoft-365).

entra.notes: Power BI is a first-party Microsoft service on the tenant's own Entra ID: users sign in with their Entra account and licences are assigned to Entra users or groups. There is no separate Entra gallery app (no Power BI entry in the Entra SaaS app tutorials index).

fallbacks.other_sync: Native Microsoft Entra ID identity; licences assigned to Entra users or groups in the Microsoft 365 admin center or Azure portal; self-service sign-up with a work account.
